545	### F-2. `autosave_gate`
546	
547	The `autosave_gate` formula is defined as:
548	
549	`refractory_block = (last_recover_T ≠ none) AND (T − last_recover_T) < W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE; hard_block = (EXISTS seat IN bound_seats: loco_state(seat) IN {DOWNED, DEAD}) OR kernel_state NOT IN {RUNNING, PAUSED} OR writer_busy OR restore_pending OR refractory_block; graph_tell_block = EXISTS d IN graph.failures(): d.subject_kind IN {NODE, EDGE, SEAM} AND d.cause == ENDOGENOUS AND d.sev ≥ 1 AND d.warn_elapsed < W_MIN_STEPS; attention_tell_block = tell_active AND (gate_tell_mode == STRICT OR tell_remaining < W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE); tell_block = graph_tell_block OR attention_tell_block; vitals_block = EXISTS seat IN bound_seats: vitals_state(seat) ≥ CRITICAL; assembly_breach_block = ragged_breach_open(); soft_block = tell_block OR breach_phase ≠ CALM OR (EXISTS seat: loco_state(seat) IN GATE_SOFT_STATES) OR vitals_block OR assembly_breach_block; waited = T − due_first_T; next_retry_T = (fail_n == 0 ? 0 : last_fail_T + min(AUTOSAVE_RETRY_TICKS × 2^min(fail_n − 1, 16), AUTOSAVE_FAIL_BACKOFF_MAX_TICKS)); fire = due AND waited mod AUTOSAVE_RETRY_TICKS == 0 AND T ≥ next_retry_T AND NOT hard_block AND (NOT soft_block OR waited ≥ AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS); risky = fire AND soft_block; risky_cause = the members of {GRAPH_TELL, ATTENTION_TELL, BREACH_PHASE, SEAT_STATE, VITALS, ASSEMBLY_BREACH} whose input is true at the fire tick (empty iff NOT risky); quit_write = kernel_state IN {RUNNING, PAUSED} AND NOT (EXISTS seat: loco_state(seat) IN {DOWNED, DEAD}); quit_risky = quit_write AND soft_block` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
550	
551	**Variables:**
552	
553	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
554	|---|---|---|---|---|
555	| `loco_state(seat)` | enum | the nine Controller states (`IDLE`, `WALK`, `RUN`, `CARRY_WALK`, `CHANNELLING`, `STAGGERED`, `DOWNED`, `DEAD`, `IN_POD`) | `controller.state` read per bound seat (SL-13) | `DOWNED` and `DEAD` are **hard** and never in `GATE_SOFT_STATES` |
556	| `vitals_state(seat)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | enum | {OK, STRAINED, CRITICAL, FAILED} | Suit & Equipment `view(player_id).vitals_state` (SE-33, designed; the worst of the breath, warmth and integrity rungs) | `vitals_block` is true at CRITICAL or worse (Suit's cap follows it: CRITICAL is WALK_ONLY, FAILED is NONE). It is capped like every soft input and never opens a hard block |
557	| `last_recover_T` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | int tick or none | 0 … `T` | Save/Load session memory: the tick of the latest `DOWNED` → non-`DOWNED` transition of any bound seat, observed through `loco_state` (SL-13); none at boot and after every restore | Anchor of the refractory: `refractory_block` is true for `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks after it (600 at the defaults). A hard-type block that expires by itself, never shortened by the cap; it does not bind `quit_write` |
558	| `ragged_breach_open()` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | bool | {0, 1} | Modular Ship Assembly pure read (MSA-33; registered, source Modular Ship Assembly) | True while a RAGGED cut's keep-side room is still venting (its hull hole is open and its pressure band is not VACUUM) or a keep-side port is still uncapped within `RAGGED_WITHHOLD_MAX_TICKS`; capping the ports does not clear it while the room vents *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; its descriptors are exogenous, so `graph_tell_block` never sees them. An absent read counts as no breach (not blocking), logged once per process as `GATE_INPUT_ABSENT` |
559	| `kernel_state` | enum | the seven kernel states | kernel (read) | Capture is valid only in `RUNNING` or `PAUSED` |
560	| `writer_busy`, `restore_pending` | bool | {0, 1} | Save/Load host-local state | One write in flight at a time; never capture into a world about to be replaced. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* An abandoned job (SL-10) does not count toward `writer_busy` |
561	| `graph.failures()` descriptors `d` (`subject_kind`, `cause`, `sev`, `warn_elapsed`) | enum, enum, 0 … 4, int steps | `subject_kind` {NODE 1, EDGE 2, COMPARTMENT 3, SEAM 4, OPENING 5}; `cause` {ENDOGENOUS, EXOGENOUS}; `sev` 0 … 4; `warn_elapsed` ≥ 0 | Life-Support Graph `read_view.failures()` (LS-19, LS-14; designed and locked) | *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)* The Graph's published warning state. Only loaded NODE, EDGE and SEAM descriptors (COMPARTMENT and OPENING descriptors carry no `warn_since_step`, so `warn_elapsed` is 0 and counting them would defer on every cold or thin room), endogenous, with `sev` ≥ 1 and a closed fairness gate, count; WORN counts; exogenous causes bypass the Graph's gate and owe no Graph-side warning. The Graph's own window, never restated here |
562	| `W_MIN_STEPS`, `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` | int steps, int ticks | 100 at the defaults (`W_MIN_WARNING_S` × `TICK_RATE` / `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`); 6 | Graph D.11 (cited) | `d.warn_elapsed < W_MIN_STEPS` is "the gate is closed"; `graph_tell_remaining = MIN over the counted d of (W_MIN_STEPS − d.warn_elapsed) × GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`, 0 … `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks, is a diagnostic and test output and does not enter `fire` |
563	| `tell_active`, `tell_remaining` | bool, int ticks | {0, 1}; 0 … `TELL_MAX_TICKS` (1 800, Attention's, cited) | Attention SIM read view `attention.view` (designed) | Remaining warning of the soonest active **Attention** tell; an absent view counts as open and logs `GATE_INPUT_ABSENT` once per process (the Graph half is unaffected) |
564	| `gate_tell_mode` | enum | {`FAIR`, `STRICT`} | Tuning Knobs | Governs the **Attention half only**: `FAIR` defers only while the remaining warning is below the Graph's guarantee; `STRICT` defers for the whole tell. For the Graph half the two collapse into one behaviour, defer for the whole open window, because the window is the guarantee |
565	| `W_MIN_WARNING_S` | int s | 10 (registry, range 4 … 20) | Graph (cited) | The fairness minimum; `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` = 600 ticks at the defaults |
566	| `breach_phase` | enum | {`CALM`, `BREACH`, `SUBSIDING`} (a TELL reads `CALM`) | `attention.view` (designed) | Only `CALM` opens the soft gate |
567	| `GATE_SOFT_STATES` | set | subset of {`CHANNELLING`, `STAGGERED`, `IN_POD`} | Tuning Knobs | Restores drop channel progress and turn `STAGGERED` into `IDLE` (PC-17); a mid-transit state is Web Map's to restore |
568	| `due_first_T` | int | 0 … `T` | session memory: the first tick `due` was true since the last fire | Anchor of the deferral clock and the retry grid; **not** reset by gate flicker. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* Nor is it reset by a `FAILED` write: **only a `WRITTEN` capture or a restore clears it**, so the loss bound counts from the first moment the save was due, and a failed write retries on the grid under `next_retry_T` without restarting the deferral clock (the two readings gave different loss bounds) |
569	| `AUTOSAVE_RETRY_TICKS` ★, `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` ★ | int | 60 … 900 and ≤ `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` / 4, default 300; `4 × AUTOSAVE_RETRY_TICKS` … (`AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` − `AUTOSAVE_RETRY_TICKS`), static range 1 800 … 17 700, default 7 200 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | Tuning Knobs | Re-evaluation period and the cap on **soft** deferral; `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS mod AUTOSAVE_RETRY_TICKS = 0` so the cap lands on the retry grid |
570	| `fail_n`, `last_fail_T`, `next_retry_T` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | int, int ticks, int ticks | 0 … unbounded; 0 … `T`; 0 … `T` + `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_BACKOFF_MAX_TICKS` | Save/Load session memory: consecutive failed writes (reset to 0 by a `WRITTEN`), the tick of the last failure, and the earliest tick the next attempt may fire | The backoff of OQ-26 inside the formula; `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_BACKOFF_MAX_TICKS mod AUTOSAVE_RETRY_TICKS = 0` (I12) keeps `next_retry_T` on the retry grid. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* The exponent is clamped at 16 (`2^min(fail_n − 1, 16)`), because an unclamped `2^(fail_n − 1)` overflows an integer after about 55 consecutive failures, which would cancel the backoff and make every grid tick retry (AC-SL-146) |
571	| `fire`, `risky`, `risky_cause`, `quit_write`, `quit_risky` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | bool; set | {0, 1}; the closed set of SL-1 | calculated | `fire` requests `request_snapshot` at this boundary; `risky` is stored in the header; `quit_write = 0` makes `save_and_quit` return `SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED` (SL-6) |
572	
573	**Output Range:** booleans, plus the `risky_cause` set. A seat-state **hard** condition is never overridden by the cap or by a quit: a `DOWNED` or `DEAD` world is never written, so no generation file ever decodes to such a seat (the refractory is never shortened by the cap, and a quit is not bound by it) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. A seat-state hard block never expires (a revived crew reopens the gate once the refractory has run out, 600 ticks later); only soft conditions are bounded, by `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS`, and the refractory bounds itself. An interval save is never taken while an endogenous Graph warning window is open and the cap has not elapsed, so no unforced generation holds a Graph tell with fewer than `W_MIN_WARNING_S` of it elapsed *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*. A due save is postponed at most `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` beyond `due_first_T` unless a hard condition holds. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* Since the user ruling (X7, Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): OQ-40 and OQ-41 (b)) the formula carries the critical-suit input (`vitals_block`, also in `quit_risky`), Assembly's open-breach input (`assembly_breach_block`) and the post-`DOWNED` refractory (`refractory_block`, a hard-type block that expires after 600 ticks and that the cap never overrides); the fairness step-back is in F-3. After a failed write the next attempt also waits for `next_retry_T`; the cap bounds only the soft deferral, not the failure backoff.
574	
575	**Example (`FAIR`):** `last_save_T = 0`, `due_first_T = 10 800`. A tell is active with 700 ticks remaining: `700 ≥ 600`, so `tell_block = 0`; the crew is `WALK`, `breach_phase = CALM`; `fire` at `T = 10 800`, kind `AUTO`, not risky. The same state under `STRICT` is blocked at 10 800, 11 100 and 11 400 and fires at 11 700 when the tell ends. **Graph example** *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*: `W_MIN_STEPS` = 10 × 60 / 6 = 100. A cable descriptor (`subject_kind` EDGE, `cause` ENDOGENOUS, `sev` 1) has `warn_elapsed` = 47 when the interval save falls due at `T = 10 800`: `graph_tell_block = 1`, `graph_tell_remaining = (100 − 47) × 6 = 318` ticks, no fire. At the next retry tick `T = 11 100` the 300 ticks are 50 steps, so `warn_elapsed` = 97 and it is still blocked; at `T = 11 400` it is 147, the window has closed, and the save fires, kind `AUTO`, not risky. A restore from a save taken at 11 400 therefore never lands inside the first 10 s of that tell. **Cap example:** a soft block from 10 800 onward fires at `T = 18 000` (`waited = 7 200`) with `risky = 1`. **Hard example:** the crew goes `DOWNED` at 17 900: at `T = 18 000` the cap has elapsed but `hard_block = 1`, so nothing is written; `DEAD` follows at 19 700 and the stub restores the generation from `last_save_T = 0`. **Backoff example** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a write fails at `T = 18 000` (`fail_n` 1): `next_retry_T = 18 300`; it fails again at 18 300 (`fail_n` 2): `next_retry_T = 18 900`; the sixth consecutive failure waits 4 800 ticks; a `WRITTEN` resets `fail_n` to 0. **Vitals and refractory examples** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the suit is `CRITICAL` from `T = 10 000`; the interval save falls due at 10 800 with `due_first_T = 10 800`: `vitals_block = 1`, no fire at 10 800, 11 100 and so on, and the cap fires it at `T = 18 000` with `risky = 1`, `risky_cause = {VITALS}`. A seat gets up from `DOWNED` at `T = 17 700`: `last_recover_T = 17 700` and `refractory_block = 1` until 18 300; at the cap tick 18 000 `hard_block = 1` and nothing is written; at the next grid tick 18 300 `T − last_recover_T = 600`, no longer `< 600`, and the save fires (`risky = 1` if a soft input is still true).

577	### F-3. `generation_select`
578	
579	The `generation_select` formula is defined as:
580	
581	`C = [g_0, g_1, …] (non-demoted candidates that pass the pre-check, by header generation descending); window_hit = g_r.risky AND (g_r.save_kind ≠ QUIT OR VITALS ∈ g_r.risky_cause) AND (T_downed − g_r.T) ≤ DEATH_LOOP_WINDOW_TICKS; fair_hit = (T_downed − g_r.T) < W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE AND (g_r.save_kind ≠ QUIT OR VITALS ∈ g_r.risky_cause); loop_hit = g_r ≠ none AND g_r == g_0 AND (window_hit OR fair_hit); selected = g_1 if (loop_hit AND |C| ≥ 2) else g_0; demote = g_r if (loop_hit AND |C| ≥ 2) else none` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
582	
583	**Variables:**
584	
585	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
586	|---|---|---|---|---|
587	| `C` | list | 0 … `AUTOSAVE_GENERATIONS` (plus transient `.bak` leftovers) | header scan after the pre-check (SL-11) | Candidates; a second pass over demoted generations (newest first) runs only if `C` is empty |
588	| `g_r` | generation or none | — | session memory: the generation the session was last restored from; none on a campaign with no restore yet | The last restored generation |
589	| `g.risky`, `g.T`, `g.save_kind` | bool, int, enum | {0, 1}; 0 … 2^63 − 1; {`AUTO`, `EVENT`, `QUIT`} | header | `RISKY` tag from F-2; capture tick (a restore returns `T` to `g.T`); the kind, so a deliberate `QUIT` generation is never stepped back past by an unrelated death *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
590	| `T_downed` | int | `g_r.T` … `T_dead` | start tick of the `DOWNED` episode that ended in `DEAD`, observed through the `loco_state` read (SL-13) | Bounds the player's *acting* time after the restore |
591	| `DEATH_LOOP_WINDOW_TICKS` ★ | int | 1 800 … 10 800, default 3 600 | Tuning Knobs | The window of the RISKY route *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
592	| `g.risky_cause`, `fair_hit` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | string[], bool | the closed set of SL-1; {0, 1} | header; calculated | `risky_cause` keeps a `QUIT` generation's RISKY-window step-back only when it contains `VITALS`. `fair_hit` is the fairness route (user ruling X7 (b)): a fall less than `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks (600 at the defaults, strict `<`) after the restored `T`, **independent of `risky`**, and of the kind except that a `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` is exempt *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2, confirmed by R15)*; it never exceeds the RISKY window (invariant I13) |
593	| `g_r == g_0` | bool | {0, 1} | calculated | The loop test: if a newer non-demoted verified generation exists, the gate opened after the restore and the player got out; there is no loop |
594	| `selected`, `demote` | generation or none | `C` or none | calculated | `selected = none` only if `C` is empty and the second pass is empty: `SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE` |
595	
596	**Output Range:** `g_0`, `g_1` or none. The result is always the newest non-demoted generation that passes the pre-check, except when `loop_hit` forces `g_1`. A load makes at most `LOAD_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (default `AUTOSAVE_GENERATIONS`) pre-check attempts. If `loop_hit` and `|C| = 1`, the only candidate is restored anyway and `SL_STEPBACK_NONE_AVAILABLE` is logged. A reproduction mismatch (SL-12) is never an input to this formula.
597	
598	**Example:** ring G7 (`T = 40 000`, `RISKY`), G6 (`T = 29 000`), G5 (`T = 18 000`); the stub restores G7, so `g_r = G7`. The crew is `DOWNED` at `T = 41 200` and `DEAD` at 43 000: `T_downed − g_r.T = 1 200 ≤ 3 600`, `g_r == g_0`, so `loop_hit`; G6 is selected and G7 is renamed `gen_k.demoted`. A second death before any new autosave selects G6 again, never G7 (it is demoted). 752	## Edge Cases
753	
754	Each case names the exact outcome and, where one exists, the diagnostic id. Diagnostics (`SL_*`) are log and `save_status` entries; they are not a second refusal set — the closed refusal set is `SL_PRECHECK_*` (T-5) and the boot set is `SL_BOOT_*` (SL-15). Cases are grouped by theme; a rule id in parentheses names where the behaviour is defined. **Reading rule for every case:** the kernel is never touched by a file the pre-check refuses, and the previous generations are never changed by a failed write.
755	
756	### Zero, maximum and out-of-range values
757	
758	- **If `world_seed` is 2^63 or above, or `T` exceeds 2^53**: the header stores each as exactly 16 lowercase hex characters and the round trip is bit-exact (F-10); a signed GDScript read of a `world_seed` above 2^63 − 1 is negative [UNV] and must still round-trip. Any other width, an uppercase letter or a non-hex character is refused (`SL_PRECHECK_HEADER_HEX_MALFORMED`, CORRUPT). Rationale: S-1 — a float parse loses everything above 2^53.
759	- **If a header number that must stay a number (`generation`, a length, an offset) arrives at or above 2^53 or with a fraction**: the float parse has already rounded it, so the pre-check refuses (`SL_PRECHECK_HEADER_FIELD_NOT_INT`, CORRUPT). Rationale: a silently rounded `generation` would corrupt ring order.
760	- **If `header_len` is 0, a corrupt 4 GiB, or larger than the file allows**: refused at the `header_len` bounds step before any allocation (`SL_PRECHECK_HEADER_LEN_INVALID`, CORRUPT). Only a re-signed file can reach this step, because the trailer step comes first; the fuzz includes re-signed files for exactly that reason.
761	- **If the encoded file would exceed `MAX_SAVE_BYTES`, a block exceeds `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES`, or the header exceeds `MAX_HEADER_BYTES` at write time**: no file is produced (`SL_WRITE_TOO_LARGE{block}`), `save_status` reads `FAILED`, the ring is untouched and play continues; nothing is truncated. Rationale: the write side never produces a file its own read side would refuse (F-6).
762	- **If the size crosses `SAVE_SIZE_ALARM_BYTES`**: the write proceeds and `SL_SIZE_ALARM` is logged once per campaign open. Rationale: it is a prompt to review compression at VS-A, not a failure.
763	- **If the header `codec` is not 0**: refused at the `format_version` step (`SL_PRECHECK_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED`, INCOMPATIBLE). Rationale: the field is reserved with no decode path in the MVP, which also rules out decompression bombs.
764	- **If `T < last_save_T` is observed**: `elapsed := 0`, `last_save_T := T`, and `SL_AUTOSAVE_CLOCK_REGRESSION` is logged once. Rationale: unreachable after the reset-on-restore rule, so it is a defect signal; dev builds assert.
765	- **If `kernel.clock.T` cannot be read as an integer**: `SL_BAD_CLOCK`, no write and no restore. Rationale: every interval and window is in ticks (SL-23); with no clock, no decision is safe.
766	
767	### Simultaneous rules and same-tick collisions
768	
769	- **If a Graph warning window opens on the tick the interval falls due, or a second window opens as the first closes** *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*: the save waits (`graph_tell_block`, F-2), re-evaluated on the retry grid; chained windows are bounded by `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS`, after which the save fires tagged `RISKY`. Rationale: the Graph's `W_MIN_WARNING_S` guarantee must not be shortened by a restore, and the cap keeps `loss_ticks` unchanged.
770	- **If the only open Graph window belongs to a dormant section**: its `warn_since_step` is frozen (Graph dormant-section rule) so it cannot close; until the Graph owner answers OQ-38 the save can wait to the cap and be tagged `RISKY`. Rationale: a rare, bounded exposure that is recorded rather than hidden.
771	- **If an event and the interval fall due on the same tick**: one save, kind `EVENT` (F-1). Rationale: the ring must not be flushed by two generations a frame apart.
772	- **If a due autosave falls inside the post-`DOWNED` refractory** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: it waits (`refractory_block`, F-2) and fires on the first retry-grid tick at or after `last_recover_T + W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE`; the cap does not shorten it, and a `QUIT` is not bound by it (SL-6). Rationale: a recovery reopens the gate onto a seat that may still be in the state that downed it (user ruling X7 (c)).
773	- **If a seat's `vitals_state` is `CRITICAL` when the save falls due and stays so past the cap** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the save defers to `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` and is then written `RISKY` with `risky_cause` containing `VITALS`; nothing is drawn. Rationale: SL-5 row (c) is capped like every soft input, so a suit that never recovers cannot suppress saving forever.
774	- **If an `ASSEMBLY_CUT` event is latched while `ragged_breach_open()` is true** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the event is not due and stays latched, the interval save is deferred as a soft input meanwhile, and the event is taken once the read turns false, that is until the keep-side cut room has vented (Assembly's read, band VACUUM) and its keep-side ports are capped or the port ceiling has passed (F-1, F-2; user ruling D54) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Rationale: a restore from a save inside a self-inflicted decompression can reload the player into an unwinnable breach that the autosave hides; the interval path is bounded by the cap; a window that outlasts it (a keep-side room open to a large connected volume) writes the interval save `RISKY` with `ASSEMBLY_BREACH`.
775	- **If a due autosave and the `DEAD` tick share a boundary**: no snapshot is taken; `DEAD` is a hard condition and the restore wins (SL-7). Rationale: a snapshot of a dead world is the trap the gate exists to prevent.
776	- **If no `DOWNED` episode was observed before `DEAD`**: `T_downed := T_dead` for `generation_select`, and the hard condition still closes the gate at that boundary. Rationale: the formula must not depend on an observation Save/Load may not have made.
777	- **If `request_restore` arrives while the kernel is `SAVING`**: the kernel waits for the boundary (K:651) and the capture completes; the death stub then settles the writer (SL-7): the new generation is a candidate only if its write has reached `WRITTEN` by that boundary, otherwise its job is abandoned. The combination should not occur at all, because `DOWNED` precedes `DEAD` by 1 800 ticks on the timer (at least `GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS` after a `give_up`) and the hard gate refuses captures while a seat is down; seeing it is a defect signal. Rationale: no main-thread wait on a write job, so a hung worker cannot hold the death stub *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
778	- **If a Save & Quit and an interval autosave are due at the same tick**: the `QUIT` path wins and the pending autosave state is discarded (`due_first_T` is session memory only); only an in-flight write delays it. Rationale: the quit writes the current state anyway.
779	- **If Continue is pressed while the kernel is `LOADING` or while the epoch staging step is pending (`restore_pending`, SL-23 (2))** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated rulings R13, R14)*: the second call is ignored (`SL_LOAD_REENTRANT`), as the kernel also ignores and reports a second request. Rationale: one restore at a time, at most one `restore_epoch` step (none on a carried Continue of the newest `QUIT` generation, R13).
780	- **If the death stub fires before the initial `NEW_GAME` generation is `WRITTEN`**: the stub finds the baseline job `WRITTEN` (then it is the candidate) or settles it as in SL-7: a job still busy is abandoned, there is no candidate, and the escalation of SL-18 applies (`SL_NEW_GAME_NO_BASELINE`, the empty directory removed, the menu); a `FAILED` baseline takes the same path *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Rationale: the 30 s `DOWNED` floor (3 ticks, 0.05 s, after a solo `give_up` in TAP mode, user ruling D7 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*) makes the case nearly unreachable, but a campaign with no verified generation must never reach a first death.
781	
782	### Writing, crashing and recovering (save/restore)
783	
784	- **If the process is killed during `WRITING_TMP`**: the position's file is intact and a partial `gen_k.tmp` remains; the next open deletes the `.tmp` and the ring is unchanged (T-6). Rationale: an unverified `.tmp` is never a candidate.
785	- **If the process is killed between `SWAPPING_OUT` and `SWAPPING_IN`**: `gen_k.bak` and a complete `.tmp` exist with no `gen_k.sav`; recovery promotes the `.tmp` if it verifies and deletes the `.bak`, otherwise promotes the `.bak` back (T-6). Rationale: at least two verified generations exist during any swap because `AUTOSAVE_GENERATIONS` is at least 2.
786	- **If a `store_*` call returns false, a file will not open, or disk is full or locked**: the `.tmp` is removed best-effort, previous generations are untouched, `save_status` reads `FAILED` (`SL_WRITE_FAILED{step}`), `last_save_T` is unchanged so the save stays due, and the retry backs off to at most `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_BACKOFF_MAX_TICKS`; after `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_ESCALATE_COUNT` consecutive failures the HUD notice is raised. Rationale: sourced — `FileAccess.store_*` returns `bool` since 4.4 (breaking-changes), so every return is checked.
787	- **If a rename fails with a sharing violation (antivirus, indexer)**: the worker retries `RENAME_RETRY_COUNT` times, `RENAME_RETRY_DELAY_MS` apart, then rolls back by renaming the `.bak` back and reports `FAILED`. Rationale: the design assumes only that renaming a closed file to an absent name is all-or-nothing [UNV].
788	- **If a write job outlives a restore**: a job that sees an advanced `write_epoch` before its first rename aborts and removes its `.tmp` (`SL_WRITE_ABORTED_RESTORE`); a job already past `SWAPPING_IN` lands a verified generation of the abandoned timeline, which is moved to `quarantine/` as `STALE_EPOCH` and is never a candidate. An **abandoned** job (SL-10) leaves `writer_busy` at once, its `.tmp` carries the old `write_epoch` in its name and its ring position stays claimed until it reports; a later autosave goes ahead on another position *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Rationale: otherwise a later death would restore the ghost of the previous timeline.
789	- **If `slot_epoch.bin` is missing or fails its CRC32, or its write fails or times out before a restore** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14)*: a missing or corrupt file reads as `max(the newest verified generation's header copy, 0) + 1`, logs `SL_EPOCH_FILE_REBUILT` and is rewritten by the worker; a failed or timed-out write lets the restore proceed with the advanced value in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE`, sets `save_status = FAILED` and is re-attempted with the next write job (SL-23 (2a), (2b)). Rationale: on the success path the epoch never goes backwards, and a failing device must not block play; the failure path is a listed exposure (OQ-25).
790	- **If two files carry the same `generation` (a kill between renames)**: prefer `.sav` over `.bak`, then verified over unverified; the loser is removed only after the winner verifies. Rationale: order is the header number, so the choice is deterministic.
791	- **If `campaign.json` is missing, corrupt or disagrees with the files**: it is rebuilt by scanning headers (`SL_MANIFEST_REBUILT`) and a load is never refused for it; demoted and quarantined generations stay excluded because they are encoded in file names, while `suspect` counters and REBASED baselines are lost. Rationale: the manifest is a hint, never truth (SL-3).
792	- **If `AUTOSAVE_GENERATIONS` shrinks between builds (3 → 2)**: the writer only uses positions `0 … N − 1`; a file at a position beyond `N` stays on disk as a candidate by generation order and is removed only by the campaign delete. If it grows, new positions fill lazily as the first free position. Rationale: never delete a file that cannot be proven obsolete.
793	- **If a restore moves `T` backwards**: `last_save_T := T(g)`, `due_first_T` and `event_pending` are cleared and `restored_gen_id := g`; generation numbers keep rising and the first new autosave is `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` after `T(g)`. Rationale: timers are sim time and the sim just went back.
794	
795	### Hostile, damaged and foreign files (pre-check)
796	
797	- **If a file is empty, shorter than the size floor, or truncated anywhere**: `SL_PRECHECK_FILE_TOO_SMALL` or `SL_PRECHECK_FILE_SHA_MISMATCH` (CORRUPT); the file is a quarantine candidate and the loader falls back. Rationale: a missing or short trailer is truncation, detected for free.
798	- **If one bit flips in the last byte of the magic (the layout-id byte)**: the trailer no longer matches, so the file is CORRUPT (`SL_PRECHECK_FILE_SHA_MISMATCH`), not INCOMPATIBLE, and the loader falls back on an intact ring. Rationale: the layout id is judged only after the trailer (SL-1 format law); a flipped bit must not stop the loader.
799	- **If one bit flips in `format_version`**: the same — corruption, falling back — never "made by a newer build". Rationale: the integrity steps precede the compatibility steps.
800	- **If the newest generation is genuinely newer (a re-signed `format_version` above ours, or `min_reader_version` above ours)**: INCOMPATIBLE — the loader stops with "made by an incompatible build", files stay in place, and the campaign directory is `READ_ONLY` for the older build; New campaign creates a different directory. Rationale: a silent fallback would roll the player back and then overwrite newer files (SL-11).
801	- **If an older generation is loadable but the newest is INCOMPATIBLE**: no fallback occurs and no older generation is overwritten. Rationale: same-campaign files share the incompatibility in practice, and a rollback is data loss.
802	- **If a block id is unknown and not on `RETIRED_BLOCKS`**: INCOMPATIBLE, the loader stops (`SL_PRECHECK_UNKNOWN_BLOCK`), so the kernel's `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BLOCK` is unreachable — reaching it would be a Save/Load defect. If it is on `RETIRED_BLOCKS`, it is stripped with `SL_PRECHECK_RETIRED_BLOCK_STRIPPED` and the mode becomes REBASED (cause 2). Rationale: a removed block must not strand old saves; an unknown one is a newer or foreign build.
803	- **If a non-mandatory block is missing and its `added_in_format` exceeds the file's `format_version`**: `default_state()` fills it with a note and the mode becomes REBASED (cause 3); otherwise `SL_PRECHECK_MANDATORY_MISSING` (CORRUPT). Rationale: K:645 leaves the decision to Save/Load.
804	- **If a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, or a block of the wrong `persist_scope`, appears in a file**: `SL_PRECHECK_PERCEPTION_BLOCK_PRESENT` or `SL_PRECHECK_SCOPE_MISMATCH` (CORRUPT). Rationale: Save/Load never writes one, so presence is a defect or tampering, and a PROFILE block inside a world file could roll knowledge back.
805	- **If a payload contains an `Object` marker, a forbidden type, excessive nesting or too many nodes**: `SL_PRECHECK_BLOCK_TYPE_FORBIDDEN` or `_BLOCK_DECODE_LIMITS` (CORRUPT); no object is instantiated and the kernel is never touched. Rationale: the object-disallowed decode stops instantiation but does not itself bound allocation (SL-2).
806	- **If a Graph payload stores a packed array as a JSON-style number list (an S-1 violation that survives the container)**: it passes the container checks, because the pre-check validates declared types, and the Graph's two-phase `restore()` refuses it (`GRAPH_RESTORE_BAD_TAG`) with the live Graph block byte-identical; the kernel enters `FAULTED` (blocks restored earlier in `restore_after` order are not rolled back, K:650), the menu offers Continue on the remaining candidates (SL-22), and the generation's failure counter increments. Rationale: owner-level validation cannot run before the kernel is touched; the 1,000-mutation fuzz (re-signed files) measures how rare this path is.
807	- **If header `T` or `world_seed` differs from the `kernel.clock` block although every hash is valid (a re-signed file)**: `SL_PRECHECK_HEADER_CLOCK_MISMATCH` (CORRUPT). Rationale: the header copy exists for exactly this cross-check.
808	- **If a file's `campaign_id` differs from its directory name (a file copied between campaigns, or a directory renamed)**: `SL_PRECHECK_CAMPAIGN_MISMATCH` (CORRUPT), quarantine candidate. Rationale: a copied directory under the same name from another machine is untrusted data under the same caps and loads if it passes; a renamed one does not.
809	- **If the header `hash_algo` is not implemented by this build**: the file stage still runs (SHA-256 is Save/Load's own), the compare is skipped (`SL_VERIFY_ALGO_SKIPPED`) and the mode is REBASED (cause 4); it is never a refusal. Rationale: a kernel hash change must not break saves (SL-16).
810	- **If stale `.tmp` or `.bak` files exist when a campaign opens**: the recovery scan of T-6 reconciles them before the first load; nothing it cannot prove obsolete is deleted. Rationale: a crash can leave any of them.
811	- **If `seats` names a PlayerId the session has not bound**: allowed; the kernel rebuilds the entity half of the binding table from the restored blocks (CR-7); the peer half is the session's *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; the owners' restores decide. A `PER_PLAYER` key outside `seats`, or an empty or duplicated `seats`, is `SL_PRECHECK_SEATS_INVALID`. Rationale: identity is the seat, never the transport peer.
812	
813	### Death stub and generation selection (degenerate strategies live here too)
814	
815	- **If a write job is still busy at the `DEAD` boundary (a hung worker)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: it is abandoned (`SL_WRITE_ABANDONED_AT_DEATH`), `write_epoch` advances, the stub selects among the already-verified candidates, and a later autosave runs on a fresh job with epoch-named temporary files; if the stuck worker ever resumes, its late rename is quarantined as `STALE_EPOCH` (AC-SL-130). Rationale: a join on a hung write would hang the frame, and a blocking wait with no timeout is not available on the engine's thread API.
816	- **If the only candidate is `RISKY` and a loop is detected**: it is restored anyway and `SL_STEPBACK_NONE_AVAILABLE` is logged. Rationale: the user rule is restart from the last autosave; there is nothing older.
817	- **If a `RISKY` generation is restored, the crew dies inside the window, and the predecessor is chosen**: the `RISKY` file is renamed `gen_k.demoted`; a second death before any new autosave restores the predecessor again, never the demoted one (the three-death scripted fixture). Rationale: without demotion the ring would oscillate between a `RISKY` newest and its predecessor.

content.thinking: I'm noting a couple of garbled details around the downed floor timing and restore requests arriving during save, plus the directory copy/rename behavior, then moving on to review lines 818-895.

content.content:
818	- **If the newest generation is not `RISKY` and the crew dies repeatedly at the same spot** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the newest is restored every time (the user rule) unless a fall comes within `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks of the restore, when the fairness route steps back whether or not the generation is `RISKY` (a `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` excepted: it is restored again, R15) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R15)*; `deaths_per_restored_gen` is counted in diagnostics for playtest. Rationale: the general step-back from a non-`RISKY` generation is the question left to playtest (OQ-1); only the fairness window was ruled (X7 (b)).
819	- **If every candidate fails the pre-check**: `SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE` is published before the kernel is touched; the Chart Table shows it as a boot-flow screen (no pause is requested, CT-25; in-session teardown, OQ-42) with New campaign or Quit; no file is deleted and the dead world is never autosaved. Rationale: the game stays inside the player's control and the files stay available for recovery.
820	- **If only demoted generations remain loadable**: a second pass restores the newest demoted one. Rationale: a stepped-back-from file is still better than nothing.
821	- **If the stub fires on a campaign with no restore yet (the first life)**: no loop is possible (`g_r` is none) and the newest generation, the `NEW_GAME` baseline at worst, is restored. Rationale: the formula needs a restored generation to detect a loop.
822	- **If the crew goes `DOWNED` within `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` (600) ticks of a restore, or later** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: within 599 ticks of `T(g_r)` the fairness route steps back (F-3: the generation is demoted, the predecessor is restored, `SL_STEPBACK_NONE_AVAILABLE` if there is none), a `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` excepted: it is restored again (R15) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R15)*; from 600 ticks on, even inside `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS`, the same non-`RISKY` generation is restored again and the loop rule does not apply. Rationale: under ten seconds of acting time is the unfair case; beyond it only a `RISKY` generation is suspected of being unwinnable.
823	- **If deaths follow a restore by under 600 ticks again and again** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: each death steps one generation further back (the generation stepped back to becomes `g_r` and the test repeats), bounded by the ring and ending at `SL_STEPBACK_NONE_AVAILABLE` on the last candidate. Rationale: every step costs the player a death and more lost time, so it is a price and not a prize; see the deliberate-fast-death case under degenerate strategies.
824	- **If the player ends the `DOWNED` wait with the solo `give_up` action** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (user ruling D7): `DEAD` follows at the apply tick, at least `GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS` after `T_downed`; the stub, `T_downed` and the selection are identical to the timer path, and a write job still busy is abandoned (SL-7). The loss floor is `GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS + 1` (F-7) and metric M2 counts the death, with `death_via_give_up` logged as a separate column. Rationale: the Controller owns the action; Save/Load sees only `DEAD`.
825	- **If a seat reaches `DEAD` in the pod** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (statuses run in the pod, user ruling D60): the path is identical: the hard gate was closed while the seat was `DOWNED`, the stub restores the newest verified generation, and `web.state` restores the leg and the pod. `IN_POD` is a soft state (SL-5), so a generation written earlier in the leg restores the in-leg state. Rationale: Save/Load keys on `loco_state` only.
826	- **If `DEAD` is entered during a camera cut**: the stub starts at that tick's boundary and the request follows its epoch staging (R14) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14)*, the Presenter holds the down sheet's last frame, and no second cut is issued (the Controller's edge case). Rationale: only `DEAD` during a *cut channel* is impossible, because `DOWNED` precedes it by 1,800 ticks on the timer (at least `GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS` after a solo `give_up`, user ruling D7) and clears the channel *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
827	- **If an owner's `restore()` or `post_restore()` fails inside `LOADING`**: the kernel enters `FAULTED` with the prior state not intact; the loader does not retry in line; the menu's Continue re-runs the pipeline on the remaining candidates (SL-22). Rationale: the kernel allows only an explicit user restore or new game out of `FAULTED` (K:170, state table) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*.
828	- **If a reproduction mismatch is detected (EXACT mode)**: release marks the generation `suspect` and plays on; dev and test halt; the loader never walks to another generation. Rationale: the bytes are proven, the defect is in the code, and it would reproduce on every generation.
829	- **If the compare window is missed (`kernel.clock.T` ≠ header `T`)**: `SL_VERIFY_WINDOW_MISSED`, no verdict, play on. Rationale: a hash taken after a tick has run would differ for the wrong reason (SL-12).
830	
831	### Save & Quit and window close
832	
833	- **If a Save & Quit is requested while any bound seat is `DOWNED`**: nothing is written — `save_and_quit` returns `SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED`, `save_status` is unchanged, and shutdown proceeds after the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving"; Continue then restores the newest verified generation. Rationale: no file on disk may ever hold a `DOWNED` or `DEAD` seat; the death stub would have restored the same file within `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS`.
834	- **If a Save & Quit is requested while a seat is `DEAD`**: unreachable in the solo MVP (the stub fires on the `DEAD` tick); the clause exists for multi-seat futures. Rationale: SL-6.
835	- **If a Save & Quit is requested with only a soft condition closed (a tell, a breach phase, `CHANNELLING`, `STAGGERED`, `IN_POD`, a `CRITICAL` suit, an open self-inflicted breach)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the generation is written immediately and tagged `RISKY` with its `risky_cause`; inside the post-`DOWNED` refractory with a healthy suit it is written and is not `RISKY`. Rationale: refusing to quit traps the player; quitting without writing silently discards up to one interval.
836	- **If a Save & Quit finds the state hash equal to the newest generation's (same `T`, nothing changed)**: the write is skipped (`SL_QUIT_DEDUPED`) and shutdown proceeds. Rationale: a duplicate generation would only push a useful one out of the ring.
837	- **If the Save & Quit write fails or times out (`SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS`)**: the quit is held, `save_status` reads `FAILED`, the pause panel stays, and the player may retry or quit without saving by hold-to-confirm. Rationale: never silently lose progress; never trap the player.
838	- **If the window is closed while a write is in progress** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the quit waits up to `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS` (frame-polled, SL-6), then **holds**: `save_status` reads `FAILED`, `quit_held` is published and the player leaves only through the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving"; the next open reconciles by the crash table (T-6). `quit_write_active` is true while the quit waits; after the timeout it clears and `quit_held` is published; `cancel_held_close()` cancels the held close (SL-21) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6)*. Rationale: one outcome for a failed or slow quit, the one SL-6 and AC-SL-45c already state; an exit after a timeout would silently discard up to one interval.
839	- **If the window is closed while the kernel is `PAUSED` under the open Chart Table (SOLO)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass)*: Save/Load's handler runs `save_and_quit()` from `PAUSED` (`PAUSED → SAVING → PAUSED`) under SL-6's rules, then `request_shutdown`; the Chart Table calls nothing (EC-CT-38). **On a boot-flow screen** nothing is written and the process ends through boot code (ASK-CT-11). Rationale: one save path, the same rules everywhere.
840	- **If a quit is requested while the kernel is `FAULTED`**: no write is attempted (K:151); the quit proceeds to the menu or shutdown. Rationale: the faulting session is never saved over an existing generation.
841	- **If the window is closed while a seat is `DOWNED`, while the kernel is `LOADING`, or while it is `SAVING`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `DOWNED` writes nothing and holds the close for the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving" (`SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED`); `LOADING` defers the close intent until the kernel is `RUNNING` and then handles it as a `RUNNING` close; `SAVING` lets the in-flight job reach `WRITTEN` or `FAILED` and then dedupes against it or writes the `QUIT` generation (SL-6, close mechanism; AC-SL-44b). Rationale: every state has one answer and none of them is a silent exit.
842	- **If a Save & Quit is made while a Graph warning window is open** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the generation is written at once and tagged `RISKY`; Continue restores a fault with less than `W_MIN_WARNING_S` of its warning left. It is not clamped (a clamp would trap the player at the menu to protect a window they can see) and it is counted by metric M4. Rationale: SL-6.
843	
844	### PROFILE store
845	
846	- **If `profile.sav` is absent and zero PROFILE blocks are registered (every MVP build)**: this is valid on a cold open — an empty profile. Rationale: nothing to restore, nothing to refuse.
847	- **If `profile.sav` is absent and one or more PROFILE blocks are registered**: `SL_PRECHECK_MANDATORY_MISSING` for the profile file (CORRUPT class); `profile.sav.bak` is tried first, and if it is also unusable the world still loads, the profile is reset to `default_state()` with `SL_PROFILE_RESET`, and the damaged file is quarantined, never deleted. Rationale: Pillar 5 says knowledge is not lost with the ship, and a corrupt knowledge file must not strand the world.
848	- **If a PROFILE write is pending when a world restore occurs**: the profile is flushed first (its file is not part of the restore) and the restore then proceeds; a world restore never reads `profile.sav` into WORLD blocks. Rationale: CR-18 — partial restore within a scope is unsupported, and PROFILE blocks are never rolled back by a world restore.
849	- **If the process is killed during a PROFILE write**: the crash table (T-6) applies to `profile.sav` and its permanent `.bak`; the ring is unaffected. Rationale: a profile is rewritten by the same atomic procedure.
850	
851	### Hallucination interplay (Pillars 1 and 4)
852	
853	- **If a save is captured while a hallucination is active**: the file holds the true SIM state — the sanity level and the owner's counters — and never the perception output (`PERCEPTION_OUT`) or a field describing what the player saw. Rationale: a save is ground truth (H1); the rebuilt output after load derives from level and seed.
854	- **If the crew reloads after dying to a scrubber that "looked fixed" because of a false system state** *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*: Save/Load restores every persisted counter and seed exactly (kernel G4, D.10), reads no perception and varies nothing by it; whether the false state's onset replays at the same moment or is re-keyed is Sanity & Hallucination Rules' decision (OQ-37). The physical fact underneath, that the scrubber fails at minute four, is unchanged and is Pillar 1. Rationale: binding perception replay here would let the player memorise hallucinations across deaths (P2, P4); any re-keying must not be steerable by quit or death. Threat draws (the ambush replayed at the same corner) are re-keyed per restore epoch by user ruling D16 (OQ-47, SL-23): the physical fact replays, the ambush does not *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
855	- **If the sanity level was low at death**: the restore returns the generation's sanity level (WORLD-scoped) — death does not cure sanity (H3), so no "die to clear your head" exploit exists. Rationale: Suit vitals and the Sanity level roll back with the world.
856	- **If the first `RUNNING` frame after `LOADING` is presented unfiltered**: this violates H4; the requirement is routed to the Perception Filter, Sanity and Pipeline (OQ-11), and the black hold covers any rebuild. Rationale: one clean frame would be a free oracle.
857	- **If an autosave would vary its timing, or a save list its contents, with sanity**: not allowed and not built; Save/Load never reads perception (SL-24). Rationale: a lie that reached the save menu would be unfalsifiable inside the session.
858	
859	### Co-op hooks and later tiers
860	
861	- **If a guest later joins (VS-B)**: the snapshot payload is separable from the file wrapper (SL-1) and is the guest's initial transfer (CR-18); a guest's save request is the reserved `saveload.request_save` command (provisional — Co-op Session & Replication), validated on the host; no guest-authoritative block exists. Rationale: host-owned saves only.
862	- **If one of several seats is `DEAD` while others live (multi-seat futures)**: the hard condition keeps autosave closed until Failure Contract & Re-wake resolves the seat (provisional — Failure Contract undesigned), so the deferral is unbounded in that case. Rationale: recorded as a gap for VS-A/VS-B, not designed here.
863	- **If a friendly-fire death occurs (VS-B)**: the save records the `DEAD` seat's state like any death and never records blame (Anti-pillar: no PvP). Rationale: blame is Failure Contract's.
864	- **If a peer reconnects under a different transport id**: nothing in any save changes — blocks are keyed by PlayerId (SL-20). Rationale: "keyed by peer id" is a stale token.
865	- **If `TICK_RATE` differs between the build that wrote a file and the build reading it**: INCOMPATIBLE at the `tick_rate` step (`SL_PRECHECK_TICK_RATE_MISMATCH`); the kernel's `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH` is the unreachable backstop. Rationale: a save is bound to the rate that wrote it.
866	
867	### Versioning and migration
868	
869	- **If a golden v1 save is loaded by a build whose Graph migrates v1 to v2**: the mode is REBASED (cause 1), the load succeeds, the recomputed hash becomes the baseline in `campaign.json`, and the next autosave writes the new shape; the old file is not rewritten. Rationale: a downgrade followed by an upgrade must not half-migrate a file (SL-14).
870	- **If a save from a development build predates the first build given to anyone outside the project**: it may be refused with "made by an incompatible development build" — migration is an obligation only from that build on (SL-14). Rationale: the policy is Save/Load's own; the Layout open question that the Graph cites is unverified (OQ-12).
871	- **If a new persisted block is registered while dev saves exist** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: every older dev save now lacks a mandatory block and carries a different `registry_epoch`, so each is INCOMPATIBLE-dev ("made by an incompatible development build"), not CORRUPT, and none is quarantined (T-5 step 21). Rationale: otherwise each new block would quarantine every dev save as damaged and hide it from the owner.
872	- **If a new persisted block is added after the first outside build**: `format_version` increments, `min_reader_version` equals the new version, the container migration is the identity and the new block is filled by `default_state()` (SL-14). Rationale: the friction of adding a block stays constant.
873	
874	### Degenerate strategies and accepted exposures
875	
876	- **If the player kills the process (task manager, power loss) after a mistake** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: Alt-F4 and the title-bar close are not kills; they raise the window-close request and take the Save & Quit path, SL-6)*: the game falls back to the newest generation, a rewind of at most `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS + AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` = 18 000 ticks (mean about 5 400 ticks, 10 800 at most when no soft input defers the save, 18 600 on the narrow recovery-at-the-cap path, F-7; the user accepted this fault loss window, D55) — the same price as dying, minus the death floor (4 ticks with the give-up, 1,801 on the timer) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; the Continue after the kill restores an `AUTO` or `EVENT` generation and so advances `restore_epoch` (R13). Accepted and unpreventable (no write can protect against a kill); measured by M3 below (OQ-25). Rationale: both rewinds cost at most the minutes since the last autosave and nothing else.
877	- **If the player Save & Quits before a risky door, relaunches and Continues** *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*: it works as a retry of the player's inputs, and because the physical world is deterministic it can also reveal what is behind the door for up to the minutes since the last autosave. Accepted for the MVP as a bounded exposure (the user's death rule is binding; the Zomboid comparison does not carry over, because a Zomboid death is final), **but with a measurable trigger, not an open-ended "if playtest shows"**: metric M3 below. The interval is not the remedy, because a `QUIT` generation is written at the quit: the response is to keep the metric and escalate to Failure Contract & Re-wake, never deleting the `QUIT` generation (OQ-25) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. A Continue of that newest `QUIT` generation carries `restore_epoch` (R13), so the threat draws replay as well and the quit buys no re-key *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R13)*. Rationale: SL-6.
878	- **If the player dies on purpose to rewind a bad decision or to scout a room** *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*: the cost is at least `GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS + 1` = 4 ticks *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* with the solo `give_up` (1,801 on the timer) plus the time back to the last autosave, the restore also returns vitals and sanity, and in a deterministic world the physical death can reveal one visible unknown (Discovery, aesthetic priority 1) for about 3 to 5.7 minutes of sim time; threat draws re-key per restore epoch (D16), so a scouted ambush does not replay *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Accepted for the MVP; metric M2 below is the trigger *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Rationale: Pillar 5's design test — safe farming versus scarcity — resolves to scarcity, as long as scouting deaths stay rare.
879	- **If the player dies deliberately fast to step the ring back** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: a fall within `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks of a restore demotes the restored generation and restores its predecessor (the fairness route, SL-8), so a player can choose to rewind further (a `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` excepted: it is restored again, R15) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R15)*. Accepted: each step costs a death and strictly more lost time, depth is bounded by `AUTOSAVE_GENERATIONS`, and it buys only the older state, never a better one than a normal death could reach; metrics M1 and M2 see it (`deaths_per_restored_gen` and `scout_death_rate`). Rationale: the fairness route is the ruled price of never waking into an unfair fall (X7 (b)).
880	- **If the player treats event saves as checkpoints (event-scum)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a weld, cut, module cut, pod arrival or berth writes a generation (`EVENT_TRIGGERS`), so a player can learn that finishing a weld "saves" and plan a risky sortie around it, the bonfire pattern this document rejects. Accepted for the MVP with metric M5 as the trigger; the response is a data change (remove the offending trigger from `EVENT_TRIGGERS`) before touching the interval. Rationale: OQ-44, confirmed by the user (D17) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
881	- **If a save file is edited by hand and re-signed**: it loads if it passes the pre-check; integrity guards accidental damage, not tampering (host-owned, no PvP, no leaderboard). Rationale: documented scope of SL-16; a stricter trust model is a security-audit question before multiplayer.
882	
883	**Playtest triggers for the accepted exposures** *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*. Pillar 5's "loss costs ship and body" and Discovery (aesthetic priority 1) pull in opposite directions here, so the exposure is accepted with numbers attached. The constants below are playtest-protocol values, not data-file knobs, and are provisional starting values to be calibrated at the first outside build (AC-SL-94). `T_enter` is, at the MVP, the derelict-level first boarding `FIRST_BOARDED{derelict_id, T}` published by Web Map & Transit (WM-28; the dock room), not a compartment-level first entry, which no designed system tracks; a DIAGNOSTIC-only compartment-entry log (Debug Overlay, from Body section changes; never persisted) is the recorded refinement if M2 proves too coarse (OQ-25) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass)*. Wall-clock gaps come from `created_unix` file metadata and the process-start log, read by the playtest harness only, never by the sim (H9).
884	
885	| Metric | Definition | Starting threshold | Named response |
886	|---|---|---|---|
887	| **M1** `deaths_per_restored_gen` | Deaths whose restored generation is the same `generation`, counted per tester | Median across testers ≥ 3, or any tester ≥ 5 | Players are stuck on the same save, so death is too dear: lower `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` by up to 3 600 ticks (not below 5 400, OQ-19); if M1 trips again, ask the user OQ-1 (non-`RISKY` step-back) |

1032	## Visual/Audio Requirements
1033	
1034	Save/Load owns no art and no sound. Its whole visible footprint is two things drawn by other systems from the reads it publishes (SL-21), plus one thing the player must never see. This section records what is visible, what is audible, who renders it, and which art-bible rules bind it, so the owners of those surfaces inherit the constraints instead of rediscovering them.
1035	
1036	**What the player can see.**
1037	
1038	| Surface | When | Rendered by | Binding rules |
1039	|---|---|---|---|
1040	| **Failed-write notice** *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)* (a plain, non-modal mark on the suit panel; shape and placement are not designed here) | Only after `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_ESCALATE_COUNT` (3) consecutive failed writes (published as `fail_escalated`, SL-21); persists until the next `WRITTEN` | HUD & Suit Layer (designed — hud-and-suit-layer.md; shape and placement are HS-46's), under art bible 7.0 (the HUD is a suit) | HR-1: it lives on the HUD layer, never dims, fades or flickers with world light, Attention or sanity. It takes **no Flesh** (`#D9A58C`, `#B5705C`) and **no Violet** (`#8A3FD1`, `#B07BE6`): those hues are reserved for the player's sanity leaking into the world (art bible 4.4), and a mark that could take them would be a lie the player could not tell from a leak (SL-24, H5). It is never a hallucination class: a false "failed" would be an unfalsifiable lie on the one channel that must stay true. It sits on an opaque Ground plate (HR-2) and counts inside the HUD's roughly 1 % non-Ground area cap (7.0). It is tied to write health, never to the gate: it looks and behaves identically whether the gate is deferring or not, and it says nothing about when a save was or will be taken |
1041	| **Newest-record line** *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)* (main-menu Continue screen only) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | While the main-menu Continue screen is open | Chart Table (designed — chart-table-web-map-and-menus.md), through `/ux-design` | One SIM fact: the playtime of the newest generation (`SaveInfo.playtime`), read once at process start. It is **not** on the pause panel: pausing is free, so a value that changed between writes would let a player infer that a write is overdue and a tell is open, the hidden gate meter UI-1 was retired to prevent. No countdown, no "time since", no per-write mark, no gate state. Ground plate; no Flesh or Violet; never a hallucination class |
1042	| **Layer-1 black hold** during `LOADING` | From kernel `LOADING` (entered one epoch-staging frame after the `DEAD` tick on the death stub, SL-23 (2) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14)*, or after the Continue press) to the first `RUNNING` frame; bounded by `LOADING_TARGET_MS` (1 000, provisional) | Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline (`TRANSIT_HOLD`, a 120 ms fade) | Plain black on layer 1. No death screen, no text, no beat: the art bible's 2.10 "last light going out" sequence is written for the cryo re-wake and belongs to Failure Contract & Re-wake (VS-A, provisional — undesigned); the death stub does **not** render it, and must stay retire-able with no presentation change beyond what VS-A adds |
1043	| **First `RUNNING` frame after a load** | The frame after the hold | Pipeline (camera `CUT` at the pre-load `k_z`), Perception Filter (designed) | The frame must already be filtered for the restored sanity level (SL-24, H4): the black hold covers any rebuild, and a single unfiltered frame is a free oracle about a hallucination. This is a routed request (OQ-11), not a Save/Load render. After a death-stub restore the HUD adds the one plain ship-log line of UI-11 on a Ground plate (Save/Load supplies only `restore_reason` and the restored generation's playtime; no Flesh or Violet, never a hallucination class, H5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
1044	| **Menu and pause surfaces**: Save & Quit, Continue, New campaign, the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving", the corrupt-ring, no-loadable-save and incompatible-build messages | On the pause panel and main menu | Chart Table (designed — chart-table-web-map-and-menus.md), through `/ux-design` | Art bible 7.4: the pause panel is a right-third side panel on Ground over the frozen world, and **the world is not dimmed, blurred or desaturated** under it (dimming is a mask on the world, blur is a lens lie, desaturation is the sanity convention 4.4 rejected). Hold-to-confirm fills a **linear bar with a needle-mark**, never a radial wipe (7.3, HR-14). Cuts and short fades of 80 – 120 ms, no slides or bounces (7.4). Selection is the 7.2 bracket plus bezel thickening, never a Tungsten fill (7.4 menu components) |
1045	
1046	**What the player never sees.** No save-list **thumbnail** (a screenshot would capture the Perception Filter's lie, Pillar 1), no ring, spinner or percentage (a "saving…" meter would turn persistence into infrastructure in the player's face and contradict "shown in the world, never a meter"), no **death screen** (art bible 7.4 and 2.10: the alternative "a death screen with text" was considered and rejected), no "progress saved" toast, no completion or progress indicator on a campaign (no win state). **No per-write autosave mark of any kind** *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*: writes are held by the gate (an active tell, a breach phase that is not calm, a seat in `CHANNELLING`, `STAGGERED`, `IN_POD` or `DOWNED`), so a mark that appeared on every write would turn its absence into a HUD signal that danger is building and, once Attention publishes its breach phase, into a hidden Attention meter (P3: "shown in the world, never a meter"). The glyph and `STATUS_WRITTEN_HOLD_TICKS` are retired; only the write-health notice above remains. The campaign list shows only `SaveInfo` facts computed from SIM blocks: campaign id, generation kind, playtime, crew count and a depth label (provisional — derived from the node `ring` of `web.view`); `RISKY` is not shown (user ruling D82) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
1047	
1048	**What the player can hear.** **Nothing, in the MVP.** There is no save chime, no write tick, no failure sting and no load sound. Reason: any sound is attributable by the web (Pillar 3), and silence is the correct cue for an event the player should not perceive at all. If the Audio design later justifies a cue, it enters through the Audio GDD, never as a Save/Load rule, and must not be confusable with a hallucinated sound (Pillar 4). The black hold is silent in this GDD; whether ambient audio ducks across `LOADING` is the Audio and Pipeline owners' call.
1049	
1050	**Strings.** The few player-facing strings this system sources (corrupt ring, incompatible build, no loadable save, failed write, quit held, the death-restore record line *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*) are plain, factual and low-affect, in a ship-log register: no exclamation marks, no emoji, no second-person death phrase, no colour from the sane or insane palette (Player Fantasy, tone). Final copy is the UX designer's and the narrative director's.
1051	
1052	**Art bible sections that apply:** 2.10 (Crew loss — explicitly not rendered here), 4.4 (the sanity palette: Flesh and Violet reserved), 7.0 (HUD-as-suit, ~1 % area cap), 7.3 (linear hold-to-confirm bar, three motions only), 7.4 (menus: world not dimmed; no death screen), 7.7 HR-1 (HUD exemption) and HR-14 (gamepad completeness, hold-to-confirm for destructive actions). Retained-screenshot evidence for each touched screen is AC-SL-92 and AC-SL-117.
1053	
1054	📌 **Asset Spec** — Visual/Audio requirements are defined. After the art bible is approved, run `/asset-spec system:save-load-and-versioned-format` to produce per-asset visual descriptions, dimensions, and generation prompts from this section.
1055	
1056	## Game Feel
1057	
1058	The player never feels a save system; they feel what it guarantees (Player Fantasy: trust without a safety net). The feel of this system is therefore a set of **absences and one half-second**, each with an owner and a measurable target. Save/Load owns the timing of the two moments below; it owns no animation, sound or camera move.
1059	
1060	**1. A save is imperceptible.** *Feel:* the world runs continuously and the ship "just exists". *Target:* the main-thread cost Save/Load adds to the kernel's capture (`t_file_encode + t_handoff`, F-5) keeps the main-thread sum `main_hitch_ms` inside one frame at 60 Hz (`SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS` 16.7, cited); the file write, flush, re-read and rename run off the critical path (SL-10); no frame within ±2 frames of a capture start other than the capture frame itself has CPU frame work above the baseline P99 plus `SAVE_HITCH_BUDGET_MS`, and the capture frame is bounded by AC-SL-87 (`main_hitch_ms` ≤ `SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS`, one 60 Hz frame) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* (AC-SL-91; an absolute 16.7 ms cap cannot hold when the frame already spends 8 to 12 ms), and the CPU-work trace around a write is within `SAVE_HITCH_BUDGET_MS` / 2 between a gate-open run and a gate-deferring run (AC-SL-131) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *What would feel wrong:* a stutter every three minutes that teaches the player when the game saved — it would turn every autosave into a small event and hand the player a rhythm to exploit — and, for the same reason, any per-write mark: there is none, because a mark shown on every write and held by the gate would make its absence a signal that danger is building (P2, P3) *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*. *Owner:* the kernel owns capture cost; Save/Load owns the added encode and hand-off; no system owns a glyph, because none exists.
1061	
1062	**2. A death is a breath of black, then recognition.** *Feel:* "death is a bitch. It happens." The loss lands in the body of the game, not in an interface: the avatar goes `DOWNED` for up to 30 seconds (`DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` 1 800, the Controller's grief window and the real tension; the solo player may end it sooner with `give_up`, user ruling D7 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*), then the stub starts on the `DEAD` tick and restores one frame later, once the new restore epoch is durable (R14) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14)*. The player sees layer-1 black for **at least 120 ms** (the `TRANSIT_HOLD` fade; shorter reads as a flash or a glitch) and **at most about 2 s** (longer reads as a crash); `LOADING_TARGET_MS` 1 000 (provisional) is the budget inside that corridor, measured as `restart_ms` (F-8). The first `RUNNING` frame is a hard camera `CUT` at the **pre-load zoom** (`k_z` is kept), so the player's framing is unchanged and recognition is instant: *I am back at the weld. The ship is exactly as I made it. I know what is in that room now.* *What would feel wrong:* a death screen, a sting, a "you died" line (the plain record line of UI-11 is the one permitted line: it states a time, not a death, user ruling D15), a lights-out beat (2.10 is for the cryo re-wake, VS-A), a zoom reset, a menu asking which save to load, or any penalty beyond the lost minutes — each would turn consequence into ceremony or punishment. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A restore must also not release a burst of catch-up ticks on its first frame: the tick driver's wall-time accumulator is discarded on entry to `RUNNING` (K-5, adopted by the kernel, CR-1a; OQ-45 closed; AC-SL-132) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*.
1063	
1064	**3. The cost of dying is a number the designer can feel.** The player pays the minutes since the last autosave and nothing else: at the defaults the mean is about 7 200 ticks (2 minutes), each death discards at most 20 400 ticks (5.7 minutes) on a healthy writer and 24 000 after one step-back (for a death whose `DOWNED` episode is the first since the last capture; each revive-and-fall-again adds up to 1 799, F-7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and a step-back chain can cost 39 000 (10.8 minutes) of reached progress (F-7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` is the main lever of how much death hurts, together with the event set (OQ-19, OQ-44): too cheap and "safe farming" returns, which Pillar 5 rejects ("scarcity that pushes inward"); too dear and death becomes a quit. These are playtest-owned numbers, measured by the 3-person kill/continue playtest (AC-SL-94) against the triggers M1 to M6 in Edge Cases, not design of consequence.
1065	
1066	**4. The refusal, not the rescue.** The autosave gate (SL-5) is felt only as an absence: the game never records a moment it could have warned the player about, because a world in a `DOWNED` state, in the ten seconds after a recovery, with a critical suit or with a Graph warning window still open, is never recorded *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The player does **not** feel rescued — the save never buys back a mistake (no save-anywhere, SL-4) and the physical world's draws are restored exactly, so the room that killed them kills them again if they walk the same path (SL-23); threat draws re-key per death restore (D16), so the ambush does not *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; a Continue of the newest Save & Quit carries the epoch, so quitting buys no re-key (R13) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R13)*. Hallucination interplay *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*: a reload is never a cure (H3) and Save/Load adds no window onto truth; whether a false state replays at the same moment is Sanity's decision, with the constraint that death and quit offer no reroll oracle (H2, OQ-37).
1067	
1068	**5. Failure is quiet and honest.** A failed write shows the plain `FAILED` notice only after `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_ESCALATE_COUNT` (3) consecutive failures; a corrupt newest generation is a one-line ship-log message and a fall back to the one before it; an incompatible build refuses to touch the campaign. None of these ever frightens: the system's tone is the opposite of the world's.
1069	
1070	**Who owns the feel.** Black-hold timing, fade and camera `CUT`: Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera (cited). The `DOWNED` grief window (30 s, or the player's own `give_up`): Player Controller & Input. The UI-11 record line: HUD & Suit Layer *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The failure notice: HUD & Suit Layer (designed — hud-and-suit-layer.md); the main-menu newest-record line: Chart Table (designed). The re-wake beat that will replace the bare stub: Failure Contract & Re-wake (VS-A, provisional — undesigned). The filter on the first frame: Perception Filter (designed; OQ-11). Save/Load owns the numbers in this section that are its own: `LOADING_TARGET_MS`, `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS`, and `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` (the written-hold of the status read is retired). Evidence: AC-SL-84, AC-SL-91, AC-SL-93, AC-SL-131 and AC-SL-132 (retained screenshots and frame-time logs, lead sign-off).
1071	
1072	## UI Requirements
1073	
1074	Save/Load draws nothing itself. It publishes host-local reads and a host-local API (SL-21); every surface below is **drawn and laid out by another system** (HUD & Suit Layer and Chart Table, both designed — hud-and-suit-layer.md, chart-table-web-map-and-menus.md) under the art bible's HUD-as-suit grammar (7.0), the menu rules (7.4) and the hard requirements HR-1 and HR-14. This section is the requirements list those UX specs inherit. The player-facing vocabulary is fixed: **Continue**, **Save & Quit**, **New campaign**; never "load game", "slot", "checkpoint", "respawn", "save point", "game over", "you died", "progress saved" or "quicksave" (Player Fantasy, tone).

AC-SL-145 checks out since the retired reference is in GDD text itself, not shipped source, so the lint rule doesn't apply there; the campaign.json deletion case advances correctly too. AC-SL-142's fresh process behavior on QUIT generation also looks fine as I continue verifying.

I'm tracing through more edge cases around Continue/QUIT generations, checking whether a Continue after a kill without a new generation gets correctly carried through per SL-23 (5), and whether FAULT_RECOVERY always advancing holds even against the newest QUIT generation. I also want to verify the missing slot_epoch fallback rule against the new-game case where slot_epoch.bin starts at 0 and the write fails non-fatally.

But I'm now spotting a real problem: since the generation header's restore_epoch is only a snapshot taken when that generation was written, and deaths after an autosave can bump the live epoch without creating a new generation, losing slot_epoch.bin and falling back to "header copy +1" could reconstruct an epoch value lower than what was actually in use — violating the "epoch never goes backwards" guarantee and potentially causing a replay of previously-drawn threats from an earlier timeline.

The GDD does acknowledge file-loss as an accepted exposure class with a recovery rule of max(copy)+1 or +2 on Continue, but it doesn't reconcile this with its own claim that epoch never regresses on the success path — this feels like a NICE-to-flag edge case rather than a blocker, so I'll note it and move on to the next chunk, lines 1288-1400.

I'm checking that AC-HE-136's epoch calculation matches the RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE value, and confirming AC-MSA-54's fixture timestamp checks out. For SL-23, I notice it doesn't explicitly name `rng_derive_epoch` but instead describes the kernel owning a single derivation for threat draws via counter_eff, with consumers calling into it.

Now I'm compiling the findings list, mostly RECOMMENDED with a few NICE items. The first issue is a stale kernel claim in SL-6/Edge about request_shutdown only being valid from RUNNING/PAUSED/FAULTED, which contradicts kernel CR-15 allowing it from every state except SHUTTING_DOWN, plus T-1's BOOTING state also lists request_shutdown — this ties to ASK-CT-11. The second and more significant issue is a contradiction around FAULTED state writes: T-1 says "Any write" is disallowed, SL-22/SL-23 describe slot_epoch.bin staging during FAULT_RECOVERY, SL-10 says never write while FAULTED, and AC-SL-79 asserts no file is created/renamed/modified in the FAULTED campaign directory — but this conflicts with the epoch write (tmp file + rename) that happens during FAULT_RECOVERY before request_restore while the kernel is still FAULTED. I'm trying to work out whether AC-SL-79's scope (autosave/quit/snapshot paths) is actually separate from this FAULT_RECOVERY write path triggered by user Continue, since that distinction matters for whether this is a real contradiction.

I'm now reasoning through why AC-SL-79 likely isn't strictly contradicted since it's scoped to autosave-due/quit/snapshot scenarios rather than an explicit user-triggered Continue action, so my recommendation is to reword it to allow slot_epoch.bin staging specifically on explicit recovery, while disallowing generation or manifest writes, and add a corresponding acceptance criterion. I also note overclaiming language across several files about "no reroll oracle" that needs softening to reflect that death re-keys the price while quitting carries it over, a design conflict between SL-11 and the Primary path that needs a single chosen approach, missing specification for pause/Save&Quit/window-close during staging that needs a new row and AC, and a graph consumer issue where soonest_warning_remaining is now published but several related specs still treat it as open or dormant — I'm recommending adopting a loaded_only query to filter dormant entries from the graph_tell_block function. Finally, I'm flagging stale provisional event-name tags scattered across multiple registry files (SL-4, F-1, Dependencies, Edge, EVENT_TRIGGERS, AC-SL-96c, OQ-24, Interactions Web Map) that all need updating to match the current naming.

Now I'm checking a related omission where BERTHED is missing from several read lists even though web_events registers both POD_ARRIVED and BERTHED, which creates a narrower read grant in Kernel CR-15 than what AC-SL-95a actually requires — this needs fixing at the kernel contract level since the test would otherwise conflict with it. I'm also working through an issue where MSA-4 now writes pending state as NONE, meaning restore-idempotent behavior could leave assembly.state stuck at REBASE_BLOCKS, so I'm proposing dropping assembly.state from the default interaction.state set and updating the registry and related ACs accordingly. Lastly, I'm looking at a divisor-list gap for AUTOSAVE_RETRY_TICKS that omits 75, which breaks W=4 fixtures and causes a boot refusal when W_MIN_WARNING_S isn't a multiple of 5 — I'm considering either hardcoding a working R value in AC-SL-51 or deriving R_g more generally to avoid the conflict.

Several smaller NICE-level issues round out the review: a timeout range mismatch between the GDD and registry (2000–15000 vs a 3000 ceiling), a misapplied 90% rule across multiple ACs, a frame-rate math discrepancy in F-8 versus RM-DECK's 30fps assumption, an untestable pre-release-build branch in AC-SL-100 that should either be deleted or properly defined, and a batch of stale labels, garbled text, and outdated verification dates scattered through the document. I also note that the SL-23 recovery rule can theoretically return an epoch value at or below one already used, which I'm flagging as a tampering/corruption exposure worth documenting rather than a blocker, plus a couple of missing AC entries from the classification table and a naming omission for `rng_derive_epoch`.

Pulling this together for the final verdict: no BLOCKING issues found, so the overall result is APPROVED, though I need to note in the summary that the schema itself lacks a verdict field. I'm also compiling the freshness and dependency notes — missing dependencies include the Failure Contract & Re-wake and Co-op Session & Replication sections, which are undesigned but not blockers, alongside confirming other dependencies like Ship Section, Perception filter, and Adaptive audio are present and fine. Finally, I want to keep the summary concise and mention that the global settings request wasn't actioned.

But FAULT_RECOVERY must write slot_epoch.tmp and rename it to slot_epoch.bin, and reach EPOCH_DURABLE, before request_restore, while the kernel is still FAULTED (SL-22/SL-23 (1)-(2)). findings.finding: H2 promises 'quit and death offer no reroll oracle', and Game Feel 4 repeats it. Under D16 plus R14 a death-stub restore re-keys threat draws (the epoch advances), which is a priced re-roll. R13 closes only the Save & Quit path. The player-facing promise overclaims.

findings.section: SL-11 (2) L215 vs 'Primary path' L223; T-8 step 2; F-8 hot-path example, Output Range and registry load_budget expression; AC-SL-120 (carried over)
findings.finding: Two incompatible hot-copy designs coexist. L215 has the worker decode and type-walk the newest and the preceding generation, so t_read, t_decode and t_walk are 0 on the main thread. L223 keeps raw bytes on the main thread and decodes them at the DEAD tick. F-8's Output Range and the registry expression say the hot path has t_decode = t_walk = 0 on the main thread, yet the F-8 hot-path example (precheck_ms 16.7, restart 153.4 ms) bills 4 + 12 ms of decode and walk. AC-SL-120 asserts 153.4. An implementer cannot satisfy both.
findings.fix: Keep the worker-decoded design (L215), which is the ruled Option A. Delete the L223 'main thread keeps raw bytes' sentence. Recompute the F-8 hot-path example as 0.5 + 0.2 = 0.7 ms precheck, so 0.7 + 16.7 + 120 = 137.4 ms. Update AC-SL-120 and the registry output line to match.
